cases.current_utterance: The bracket is deforming too much.
Yeah.
The current bracket is 3 mm aluminum.
Maybe the thickness is causing the problem.
Okay, that makes sense.
Let's run the initial bracket deformation test with a 4 mm version.
Can you repeat that?
In the initial bracket deformation test, the 4 mm version still exceeded the deformation limit.
Please repeat that initial bracket deformation test with the 4 mm version this afternoon.
We have decided to use the 4 mm version in the next prototype.
I will reconnect in one minute.
The client requires a safety factor of two.
Maybe the support stiffness is the real issue.
Let's test the support condition next.
In the initial bracket deformation test, the 4 mm version still exceeded the deformation limit.
Now let's discuss the sensor enclosure.
The sensor enclosure wall is cracking near the mounting holes.
Can everyone see my screen?
Maybe the mounting-hole spacing is concentrating the stress.
Yeah, I can see it now.
Let's test a version with wider hole spacing.
In the test with wider hole spacing, the sensor enclosure no longer cracked.
Give me a second, I need to grab my charger.
Going back to the bracket, the afternoon rerun of the initial deformation test with the 4 mm version is complete. It still exceeded the deformation limit.
Sorry, my audio cut out for a second.
For the sensor enclosure, let's test a 4 mm wall.
The client also requires a maximum mass of 2 kg.
By the way, lunch is in the conference room.
That 2 kg limit applies to the sensor enclosure.
Separately, the bracket coating is failing the salt-spray test.
Give me a second, I'm opening the coating report.
Maybe the coating thickness is too low.
Let's measure the coating thickness.
I can't see the slides because the meeting-room projector is disconnected.
We measured the coating at 18 microns, below the required 25.
Back to the bracket deformation, let's test the support stiffness under the same load.
Can we take a five-minute break after this?
For the sensor enclosure, the 4 mm wall cracked again.
The sensor enclosure must remain under 2 kg.
The bracket must maintain a safety factor of two under the test load.
Okay.
Did anyone see the game last night?
Let's run the support-stiffness test under the same load tomorrow morning.

typed_relations.authorship: Semantic review and labels fixed before API inference. No API outputs or observed predictions were inspected for this clarified fixture.
typed_relations.preservation: Separate derivative fixture. Exactly five current_utterance values change (C06, C08, C09, C15, C24); all 43 case IDs, retention labels, event types and expected_threads remain identical to typed-relations-b002.json. Both B002 source fixtures remain untouched.
typed_relations.annotation_policy: Annotated none means a defensible absence of a useful direct link under the current taxonomy. An omitted pair has no expected label and must remain unscored, never implicitly none. All eligible pairs are accounted for by an annotation or an explicit unannotated-pair explanation.
typed_relations.candidate_scope: Only prior retained events assigned to the same thread. Pending C12 and C27 get empty maps. No cross-thread or retrospective-resolution edges are adjudicated.
typed_relations.configuration_resolution: The initial and afternoon executions are explicitly distinguished, and every changed positive setup-comparison pair explicitly identifies the bracket-deformation test and 4 mm version. Initial versus afternoon identifies executions, not incompatible physical configurations. No unstated load, support condition or other setting is filled from a plan. All unchanged configuration judgments are preserved.

unannotated_pairs.reason: The thickness reference uses the baseline fact to resolve its parameter, but the contract does not unambiguously distinguish a direct related_to edge to that property fact from background-only reference resolution. The explanatory edge to C01 is annotated separately.

The alternative support-stiffness explanation could concern the original deformation problem generally or the particular failed 4 mm experiment. The text does not identify that specific result as its explanatory target.

This names support stiffness and a load condition more precisely than the earlier support-condition proposal, but it does not say that it replaces, clarifies, repeats, or is a second execution of that proposal. A later return to a still-open plan and a new trial are both plausible.

Again explicitly signals recurrence, but the new wall version and crack location are not identified relative to the earlier mounting-hole crack. The taxonomy does not clearly specify whether recurrence of a physical fault is repeats, related_to, or merely another observation; no exact recurrence/configuration is asserted.

The 4 mm wall observation is compatible with the earlier proposed test, but the utterance does not state that a test was executed. Retain observation as supplied and do not infer a result_of edge merely from a proposal plus a later fault.

The same scoped mass constraint is restated; however under 2 kg may specify a strict inequality where 2 kg limit did not state the boundary explicitly. A plain restatement and a boundary clarification are both plausible. This is not automatic supersession or evidence of compliance.

Naming the support-stiffness test may directly express the causal investigation purpose, or may simply reference the already-proposed test C36. The direct-versus-inherited purpose link is insufficiently explicit for a unique label.

Neither proposal identifies a completed earlier execution or a unique shared test ID. The new scheduling instruction does not establish a repeated execution of the old generic support-condition proposal.

Tomorrow morning may schedule the same still-open test, reschedule it, or request an additional execution. Unlike C09, C43 does not say again. Do not force repeats, supersedes, or clarifies without that distinction.

pair_review_by_source.C01: First bracket-deformation event has no previous same-thread candidates.
pair_review_by_source.C03: Existing 3 mm aluminum design is background. It does not assert why the bracket deforms, a planned change, or a comparison with C01; C03 -> C01 is none.
pair_review_by_source.C04: An unverified explanation is explicitly offered for the deformation problem C01. This related_to edge is not established physical causation. The property-fact target C03 is left unannotated.
pair_review_by_source.C06: The initial bracket-deformation proposal explicitly specifies a 4 mm version and investigates the preceding thickness hypothesis C04. Naming the execution does not turn baseline material C03 into a replaced design or establish a separate causal claim about C01.
pair_review_by_source.C08: The explicitly initial bracket-deformation result belongs to C06, with the stated 4 mm setup. No extra conditions are invented. Failure alone neither refutes the broad thickness hypothesis nor invalidates the historical deformation observation.
pair_review_by_source.C09: The afternoon request explicitly repeats the initial bracket-deformation test with the 4 mm version. Both the initial proposal C06 and result C08 identify the prior execution, so both receive repeats/exact. Neither edge closes this newly requested execution.
pair_review_by_source.C10: The 4 mm version is chosen for a future prototype, but no evidence is explicitly cited as the rationale. Do not manufacture based_on from preceding test results, supersede the historical 3 mm fact, or treat adoption as proof that deformation was solved.
pair_review_by_source.C12: Thread assignment remains pending. No intrathread candidates, semantic edges, or retrospective assignment are inferred.
pair_review_by_source.C13: A different possible cause is offered for C01. It does not explicitly reject or replace C04, and merely being a plausible explanation of C08 is insufficient for an annotated direct edge to that particular trial.
pair_review_by_source.C14: The proposed support-condition investigation directly addresses C13. It neither cancels the earlier requested rerun nor inherits links through the hypothesis.
pair_review_by_source.C15: The initial execution is now identified. C06 receives result_of/exact; the afternoon rerun C09 and support-condition proposal C14 receive none. C08 is another report of this same initial execution: reporting it again is neither a new execution (repeats) nor a result of the earlier report (result_of), and no report-to-report comparison is asserted.
pair_review_by_source.C17: First sensor-enclosure event has no previous same-thread candidates.
pair_review_by_source.C19: The mounting-hole-spacing hypothesis explicitly offers an explanation of the cracking problem C17; it is not a proven causal effect.
pair_review_by_source.C21: The wider-spacing experiment directly investigates C19. No separate purpose edge to C17 is inherited through the hypothesis.
pair_review_by_source.C22: The reviewed text explicitly states a performed wider-spacing test, so result_of C21 is clear and their stated setup corresponds. Success alone is not an explicit causal-support claim about C19 and does not contradict the historical crack observation C17.
pair_review_by_source.C24: The completed afternoon rerun has an exact result_of link to its own proposal C09. It explicitly repeats the initial test identified by C06 and its two reports C08/C15, so those three receive repeats/exact. C08 and C15 still represent one initial execution, not multiple completed tests. These repetition links do not imply that the broad thickness hypothesis was disproved or the deformation problem resolved.
pair_review_by_source.C26: A wall-thickness experiment is proposed. This continues the enclosure thread but does not explicitly repeat, replace, explain, or rely on a particular earlier event. Shared enclosure and cracking context do not themselves create edges.
pair_review_by_source.C27: Thread assignment remains pending. No candidate set or edges, including to another pending generic requirement, are inferred.
pair_review_by_source.C29: This clearly scopes a prior mass constraint to the enclosure. Its natural clarification target C27 is pending and outside the same-thread candidate set. Do not redirect clarifies to an unrelated assigned event or use this as proof of compliance.
pair_review_by_source.C30: First independent coating investigation event. A salt-spray outcome does not create an unseen proposal event or cross-thread edge to the bracket-deformation history.
pair_review_by_source.C32: The low-coating-thickness hypothesis is an explicit possible explanation of the salt-spray failure C30, without asserting proven causation.
pair_review_by_source.C33: The proposed measurement directly tests the low-thickness claim C32. A link to C30 is not inherited through that hypothesis.
pair_review_by_source.C35: This explicitly performs the coating-thickness measurement proposed by C33; no identifying setup parameter specified by that proposal is omitted. The 18-versus-required-25 comparison directly supports the low-thickness claim C32. It does not prove that thin coating caused the salt-spray failure C30.
pair_review_by_source.C36: The named support-stiffness investigation directly tests the candidate explanation C13. Its identity relative to C14 is unresolved; returning to a topic does not establish an executed test to repeat.
pair_review_by_source.C38: Preserve the supplied observation classification. The relation to proposed trial C26 and the earlier crack occurrence C17 is not uniquely established. A 4 mm wall cracking does not contradict the earlier wider-hole-spacing result C22 without evidence that this wall used that spacing and test setup.
pair_review_by_source.C39: A scoped requirement is restated; no result verifies or violates it. Its relation to the earlier 2 kg phrasing is left unannotated because the strictness/clarification distinction is not explicit. No physical-fault relation is invented from possible engineering relevance.
pair_review_by_source.C40: This scopes the safety-factor criterion to the bracket under a load. C12 is the natural pending scope-clarification antecedent, but is not an assigned same-thread candidate. The requirement does not prove an earlier test passed, close an investigation, or explicitly modify a particular plan.
pair_review_by_source.C43: Scheduling the support-stiffness test tomorrow is useful memory, but does not establish a second execution. Preserve ambiguity relative to C36 and C14, and do not turn repetition of phrasing into a lifecycle completion or supersession.

question_interpretation_limits: In this clarified variant C15 explicitly reports the initial execution, so it can target C06 and cannot complete the afternoon rerun C09 or support proposal C14. Repeating a report of an execution is not repeating the execution.

C24 explicitly reports the completed afternoon rerun of the initial test. Its own proposal C09 receives result_of; the initial proposal and its reports can receive repeats. No result_of edge is propagated to the initial proposal merely through a repetition chain.
C43 schedules a test but does not say again. Scheduling an existing open plan is not automatically a repeats or supersedes relationship.
C38 remains an observation. A prior proposal and a later physical fault do not themselves establish performance of that proposal.
A favorable intervention outcome is not automatically explicit causal support, and a later fault under an unidentified configuration does not contradict an earlier successful experiment.
An adopted design version does not retrospectively make its failed test pass, identify the decision rationale, or close the technical problem.

typed_relations.repeat_target_policy: A repetition can directly reference either a test proposal or reports identifying the earlier execution. C09 repeats the initial trial identified by C06/C08. Only execution identity and explicit 4 mm setup wording were clarified. No category or lifecycle rule is changed to fit this fixture.
